documents.processed_text:
Chunking Strategies
Chunking splits documents into smaller pieces for retrieval. Fixed-size chunking uses equal lengths
but may break context. Semantic chunking splits by meaning (sentences/paragraphs), preserving
coherence. Recursive chunking combines both by splitting hierarchically. Choose chunk size based
on embedding context window, domain structure, and retrieval quality trade-off.
Embedding Models
Embedding models convert text into dense vectors capturing semantic meaning. They map similar
texts to nearby points in vector space using neural networks trained on large corpora.
Choosing Embedding Models
Consider domain match, multilingual support, latency, cost, and benchmark performance (MTEB).
Use domain-specific embeddings when available.
Agentic RAG
Agentic RAG introduces an agent that plans, decides when to retrieve, calls tools, and iterates. It
enables multi-step reasoning and dynamic retrieval.
Hybrid Search
Hybrid search combines vector similarity and keyword (BM25) search. It improves recall by
capturing both semantic and lexical matches.
Re-ranking
Re-ranking uses a cross-encoder or LLM to reorder retrieved documents for better relevance,
improving precision.
Multi-hop Questions
Use query decomposition, iterative retrieval, and reasoning chains to combine multiple documents.


Lost in the Middle
LLMs tend to ignore middle context in long inputs. Mitigate via reordering, chunk prioritization, and
windowing.
Evaluation
Faithfulness: answer grounded in sources. Relevance: retrieved docs match query. Context
precision/recall: quality of retrieved chunks.
Self-RAG
Self-RAG allows the model to decide when to retrieve using confidence or uncertainty signals.
Graph RAG
Graph RAG uses knowledge graphs for structured relationships. Useful for complex multi-hop
reasoning.
Structured Data
Use SQL querying, table-aware embeddings, or tools to query structured sources directly.
Failure Modes
Hallucination, poor retrieval, redundancy, latency. Debug via logging, eval datasets, and ablations.
Freshness
Use incremental indexing, streaming pipelines, and document versioning.
Latency Optimization
Use ANN indexes, caching, smaller embeddings, batching, and async pipelines.


Metadata Filtering
Filters restrict search space (e.g., user, date), improving precision and security.
RAG vs Fine-tuning
RAG is better for dynamic knowledge. Fine-tuning is better for behavior/style or static knowledge.
Query Transformation
HyDE generates hypothetical answers, decomposition splits queries, step-back abstracts intent.
Citations
Store chunk metadata and return sources alongside answers.
Scaling
Use sharding, distributed vector DBs, and ANN indexes.
Parent-Child Chunking
Retrieve small chunks but return larger parent context for better grounding.
Fix Hallucination
Improve retrieval, enforce citations, use stricter prompts, or verification steps.
Reduce Redundancy
Lower overlap, deduplicate via similarity thresholds.


Speed Retrieval
Use ANN (FAISS), caching, and filtering.
Deduplication
Cluster similar embeddings and remove near-duplicates.
Access Control
Use metadata-based filtering with user permissions.
Domain Jargon
Use domain-specific embeddings or fine-tuning.
Multimodal RAG
Add OCR, image embeddings, and multimodal models.
Versioning
Track document versions and timestamps.
Fix Multi-hop Failures
Use agents, decomposition, and iterative retrieval.
Resolve Conflicts
Rank sources by trust, recency, and consensus.


Keep Data Current
Frequent re-indexing and freshness scoring.
PDF Parsing
Use layout-aware parsers, OCR, and table extraction tools.
